lines: GOLDSKIN MINING Co. FACTORY. The LOADING BAY is off the yard, and the LOCKERS and No. 1 LINE off the LOADING BAY, the line on a shop padlock. The TIME OFFICE, the EXTRACT, the SWITCH ROOM and the PRESS HALL are off No. 1 LINE, the PRESS HALL on another padlock. The GENERATOR HALL is down the EXTRACT, and through the SWITCH ROOM from the line.

The STORES and the FOREMAN'S OFFICE are off the PRESS HALL, the STORES behind a power shutter. ASSEMBLY is through the FOREMAN'S OFFICE, and DESPATCH through ASSEMBLY; the roller door there gives on this yard. Shop keys are signed for at the LOCKERS.
The lamp runs are marked in red. All of them but one are crossed out, ruler straight, in the same ink and the same hand as the plan.
GOLDSKIN MINING Co. SAFETY. No man is to work on the line except in good light. By order.
Under it, in pencil, small and careful: they only mind what they can see. do not work in good light. The second part's been gone over twice.
CLOCK IN. CLOCK OUT. Cards are to be left in the rack at all times. GOLDSKIN MINING Co.
Every card in the rack is stamped in for today, and not one is stamped out. I look at the date twice. It's today's.
CALL BOXES. Press once for a hauler. Do not press twice. GOLDSKIN MINING Co.
Haulers take the shortest way they know to the box that calls them. They have not been told which walls are new.
Chalked on the new brickwork, in the hand from the plan: the FOREMAN'S OFFICE gate is chained into this wall. Nobody is to call a hauler.
TIME OFFICE. The stove's in, and there's a kettle on the hob, the handle still warm. The window onto the yard has been boarded up from this side.
There's no handle on the outside of the door. If it goes badly out there, this is where I'll wake.
A glass orb on a kitchen stand, wired into the generator with two lengths of bell wire. The stand's the one from the study at Julie's.
Holding it is like a door handle in winter, and it goes on doing it in my fingers for a while after I let go.
The orb's clear, and the wire's warm. The stand hasn't moved. I leave it where she put it.
Monday. Had the lamps out of No. 1 line, run by run, as the office wants. The men complain of the dark. I told them what I was told: it saves the Company money.
The line has been quieter since. I do not mean the machines.
Tuesday. Press hall lamps out as well. The night man won't walk past the loading bay now, not for time and a half.
I have taken his card out of the rack so it does not show him late. If the office asks, he was never on.
Tuesday, later. The generator is warm and I have not started it. There is a glass thing wired into it that nobody ordered, and it is on no list I hold.
I wrote to the office about it twice. The second letter came back with my own spelling corrected, and nothing else said.
The letter's folded into the page. The corrections are small and neat, and I know the slant.
The rest of the diary is sums. Nine, fourteen, nine, fourteen, down three pages, and then a column that doesn't add up to anything I can find.
LOADING BAY. The LOCKERS and No. 1 LINE off it.
Under it, stencilled: SHOP KEYS TO BE SIGNED FOR AT THE LOCKERS. NO KEY LEAVES THE WORKS.
DESPATCH. The roller door is worked from inside only, off ASSEMBLY. Nothing is to be left on the yard side after the shift.
TIME OFFICE. CLOCK IN. CLOCK OUT.
Under it, chalked: stove kept in, kettle kept full. whoever is last.
EXTRACT. The duct drops to the GENERATOR HALL.
Scratched under it with a nail, deep: nobody comes back up.
PRESS HALL. HAULERS WORKING. The STORES and the FOREMAN'S OFFICE through the hall. Stand clear of the haulers.
SWITCH ROOM. Between No. 1 LINE and the GENERATOR HALL.
The shutter runs off the generator's own supply. The generator is not running.
STORES. Power shutter. Up while the Works has power, and down otherwise.
No. 1 LINE. ONE FUSE FOR THE LINE LAMPS AND THE STORES SHUTTER.
IF IT GOES, THE SHUTTER COMES DOWN AND STAYS DOWN UNTIL THE FITTER CALLS. Under it, in pencil, twice: fitter sent for.
